title: Dạ, chào chị
englishTitle: Respectful hello to an older woman
summary: Different ways to say Dạ, chào chị in Vietnam teach the respectful older-woman greeting.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Dạ, chào chị is the respectful greeting for an older woman or adult female staff member. It is useful at cafes, hotels, shops, clinics, classes, tour desks, and anywhere the first word should show care.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use it when chị fits the person better than bạn, cô, or bà.

phrases.english: Respectful hello to an older woman

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Dạ adds respect; chị picks the older-woman relationship.

breakdown.english: respectful hello to an older woman

sections.title: Relationship swaps
sections.body: These keep the same respectful shape while changing who you are greeting.

phrases.english: Respectful hello to an older man
Respectful hello to an aunt-age woman

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it for an older female server, desk agent, shop owner, guide, nurse, teacher, or local helper when a warm respectful opener fits the moment.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Chị often sounds warmer than bạn for an adult woman who seems older than you. If she is clearly aunt-age, Dạ, chào cô may fit better.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: These phrases often follow a respectful greeting.
